items.stem: In value-proposition design, a 'pain reliever' is an element that:

options.text: Describes a feature of the product
options.rationale: A feature is not automatically a pain reliever.

options.text: Reduces a specific frustration in the customer's job
options.rationale: Correct: pain relievers address identified customer pains.
Internal cost is the cost side, not customer value.

options.text: Adds a channel to reach customers
options.rationale: Channels are a separate building block.

items.explanation: Correct: pain relievers address identified customer pains.

items.stem: Value-based pricing differs from cost-plus pricing mainly because it starts from:

options.text: The cost to produce plus a fixed margin
The value the offering creates for the customer
options.rationale: Correct: value-based pricing anchors on customer-perceived value.

options.text: The price of the cheapest competitor
options.rationale: Matching the cheapest rival is not value-based pricing.

options.text: A round number that is easy to remember
options.rationale: Memorable numbers are a tactic, not the pricing basis.

items.explanation: Correct: value-based pricing anchors on customer-perceived value.

items.stem: To test a business model fully, which TWO questions must be answered? (Select TWO)

options.rationale: Correct: desirability tests whether there is real demand.

options.text: Can we deliver and sustain it profitably (viability)?
options.rationale: Correct: viability tests whether the economics work.

options.text: Does the canvas look visually balanced?
options.rationale: Visual balance says nothing about whether the model works.

options.text: Is the idea novel to investors?
options.rationale: Novelty is not a test of model validity.

items.explanation: Correct: desirability tests whether there is real demand.; Correct: viability tests whether the economics work.
